Winners Do Things Differently

What repeated exposure to high-performing people revealed about discipline, preparation and the small choices behind visible success.

20 August 20253 min read
LearningDisciplineGrowth

Last week, Bobby and I were talking about confidence. Not the loud kind. But the kind that shows up slowly when you’ve survived long enough to grow. When you've become aware of your own strength, even in silence.

This week, we took that thought a step further.

“So… once you’ve found confidence,” Bobby asked, “What do you do with it?”

I paused. Because that’s when courage enters the picture.

Confidence makes you feel ready. Courage is what moves your feet.

And that took me back to a chapter from my early career in India.

It was early in my career in India. We were a strong team, respected, consistent, and well-known across the company. But every year, during the annual sales ceremony, where the top-performing offices were honored, we found ourselves clapping for others. Always close. Never called.

We had the talent. The trust. The reputation. But the stage? It remained out of reach.

Then came a shift, a niche product line that no one was paying attention to. Low visibility. Low expectations. Low interest. But my manager saw something others didn’t.

“What if we co-promoted this product with a major MNC?”

It had never been done before. It was risky. Different. Easy to dismiss. But he believed in it. And more importantly, he believed in us.

That belief sparked courage.

We stepped into unfamiliar territory and stayed there for nearly two years. And along the way, we met resistance, doubt, and fatigue.

Initial outreach was discouraging. Customers were polite, but hesitant. It felt like we were pushing uphill, alone. We didn’t give up. We took it one client at a time.

The first few conversions came in. Small, yes but they gave us momentum. It wasn’t validation. But it was hope.

Some questioned the focus: “Why invest so much in something unproven?” We didn’t argue. We just kept building.

Momentum picked up. Clients began to see value. Word spread. Resistance faded.

As we approached the end of the second year, things weren’t looking the way we had hoped. Despite all our effort, the revenue from this experiment was only trickling in not flooding.

There were whispers. Was this worth it? Had we overestimated the opportunity?

After two years of work, this hit hard. Because it wasn’t just a project on the line.

The long hours, the risks, the belief we’d poured into this,suddenly felt fragile.

Eventually, we crossed a major threshold, We had shifted over 50% of the segment in our favor.

That year, we became the top-selling business unit in India for that product line. I was named the Best Salesperson nationwide.

But honestly, it wasn’t about the title. Or the numbers.

For our team, the real win came the night of the annual sales ceremony.

After years of sitting in the audience, applauding others... We finally heard our office name called. We finally stood on that stage, together.

Not because we followed the norm. But because we dared to do something different, and had the courage to stay with it long enough to prove it mattered.

“So… was that your boldest move?” Bobby asked me not long ago. I smiled. “No. The boldest part wasn’t the idea. It was showing up every day, long before anyone else believed it would work.”

He nodded.

“That’s the thing about courage,” he said. “It doesn’t always feel brave. Sometimes… it just feels right.”

Over to you:

Have you ever been in a place, physically or mentally, where you weren’t sure you’d last… but eventually found your footing? Would love to hear your story. 👇
